comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from ACTA's (Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam, the joint VU/UvA dental faculty) current official overview, 'Inhoud' (content) and 'Toekomst' (career) pages for Bachelor Tandheelkunde (all checked 2026-09-27), cross-verified against the most recent standalone Onderwijs- en Examenregeling (OER) document accessible to available tools, 'Onderwijs- en Examen Regeling Bacheloropleiding Tandheelkunde 2020-2021' (s3; the document's own running header repeats an unedited '2019-2020' template artefact from the prior year's version, a known drafting quirk of this document rather than a substantive conflict). ACTA's current OER page (checked 2026-09-27) states that current-year OER content is now published only inside the dynamic studiegids.vu.nl web application rather than as a separately downloadable document; repeated attempts to retrieve the current 2025-2026/2026-2027 OER and course pages through that application returned no extractable curriculum content to available tools (dynamic client-side rendering), and no newer standalone OER PDF was found through reasonable search of acta.nl, vu.nl and third-party archives, so the 2020-2021 OER is used as the controlling formally adopted source for the exact EC/compulsory-status structure per Section 2.1. Its qualitative structure is independently corroborated by the current official pages: a three-year, 180-EC programme (s0) with an 'oriënterend karakter' first year combining dental subjects, medical basic sciences and 'wetenschapsbeoefening' (science practice) and a thematic 'blokken en lijnen' (blocks and lines) curriculum design carried through Years 2-3 with 'sterkere verwevenheid van theorie en praktijk' (s1); Article 10.2 of the OER confirms the programme has exactly one afstudeerrichting, 'Bacheloropleiding Tandheelkunde' itself (i.e. no formal sub-route to instantiate), matching the registry's generic normalized target cp-000118 (row 119, source_provider_id 111A136, recognized_programme_code 56560, programme_unit_code 1001O5917, languages_json=["NLD"]), so routeSelection is null. Article 1.2's definition of 'onderwijseenheid' fixes the credit unit; Article 11.3's compulsory-unit table sums exactly to 60 EC per year across three years (180 EC total): Year 1 (60 EC) comprises Cellen en Weefsels (4), De gezonde mond (8), Infectie en ontsteking (8), Introductie (6), Lijn introductie kliniek (1), Mens en wetenschap (5), Moleculair biologische processen (4), Orgaansystemen (8) and the five Lijn TVI (Tandheelkundige Vaardigheden I) preclinical-skills sub-units (1+1+2+2+2+8=16, sub-items of Article 11.3's table); Year 2 (60 EC) comprises Cariologie en de harde tandweefsels (7), Endodontologie (7), Functieherstel met kronen (7), Lijn tandheelkundige preventie (6), Parodontitis I (4), the Lijn TVIIA/TVIIB clinical-skills sub-units (3+3+1+1+4+4+1=17), Vorm en functie (3) and De zieke mens (9); Year 3 (60 EC) comprises Functieherstel met bruggen (4), Parodontitis II (4), Medisch tandheelkundige interactie (4), Diagnostiek (4), Tandarts, patiënt en samenleving (4), Tandarts en wetenschap (5), the Wetenschappelijke stage (16), the Lijn preventie en behandeling sub-units (6+1+3+2=12), the Lijn TVIII sub-units (2+1+1=4), Portfolio (1), Vrije studieruimte (1) and Professioneel gedrag (1). Article 11.4 confirms a genuine free elective space ('vrije keuzeruimte') of only 1 EC in Year 3, filled with faculty-designated facultative units (Canvas); this space is preserved explicitly as its own component (Vrije studieruimte) rather than instantiated with invented content, consistent with the programme's own OER-defined structure and with the current official pages' silence on any minor or broad free-choice space (unlike a generalist bachelor such as Sociologie). Article 1.2's definition of 'praktische oefening' names 'het maken van een scriptie of thesis' and 'het uitvoeren van een onderzoekopdracht' as its own examples of practical exercises; among the compulsory units, the 16-EC Wetenschappelijke stage (paired with the evidence-based-dentistry course Tandarts en wetenschap) is ACTA's own substantially-sized independent-research placement culminating in a written research report, and is therefore recorded as researchComponentId; no other single component approaches its EC weight or research framing. Article 10.3's seven named eindtermen-domeinen (I Hanteren van klinisch tandheelkundige problemen, II Wetenschappelijk denken en handelen, III Communiceren en samenwerken, IV Maatschappelijk handelen, V Organiseren van zorg, VI Tandheelkundig handelen, VII Professionaliteit) are based on the nationally adopted Raamplan Tandheelkunde 2020 competency framework, which remains ACTA's current competency basis and independently corroborates the programme's own defining domains without requiring their full eindtermen text (unavailable in the extracted document due to a broken internal cross-reference). The current official overview page (s0) independently confirms the Fall-2026 entrant cohort ('Programme start: 31 August 2026') matching the fixed UCR starting cohort used for this comparison, and states the programme combines 'science, technique and communication' around patient-centred, preventive dental care, consistent with the OER's own Domein I/III/IV/VI framing. No further official source needed to be consulted: the current official overview/content/career pages and the most recently available formally adopted OER together establish a complete, internally consistent, entirely accounted-for 180-EC pathway with explicit EC and compulsory status for every unit, an explicit basis for the null route judgment, and an explicit, UCR-independent judgment (preserving rather than instantiating the 1-EC vrije keuzeruimte) fixed before any UCR course was considered.

alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to ACTA's Bachelor Tandheelkunde (OER Article 10.2 confirms no formal afstudeerrichting beyond the generic bachelor itself for this normalized target): a biomedical-science core -- cell and tissue biology, human anatomy and physiology, biochemistry, infection and immunity, and the molecular mechanisms of disease -- combined with UCR's medical/health psychology, statistics and communication offerings to reproduce the programme's own combination of scientific biomedical training with patient-centred communication and evidence-based practice, while leaving the 1-EC vrije studieruimte honestly preserved as unclaimed elective space and the programme's entire preclinical/clinical manual-skills training (patient treatment, restorative and periodontal technique, drilling licensure and the associated Lijn TVI/TVIIA/TVIIB/TVIII testing) genuinely unmatched, since UCR provides no clinical placement, dental-manual-skills practicum or patient-treatment training of any kind.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is dominated by UCR's biomedical-science cluster (10 of 24: Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Epidemiology & Public Health, Functional Anatomy, Molecular Cell Biology, Human Physiology, Biochemistry, Life Science Laboratory, Infection & Immunity, Mechanisms of Disease, Pharmacology, Molecular Pathology & Genetics -- eleven if the gateway is separately counted), reinforced by a psychology-and-communication cluster addressing patient care (7 of 24: Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Social Psychology, Medical & Health Psychology, Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, The Art of Rhetorical Communication, Rhetoric in Action) and a light methods/societal-context thread (Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Introduction to Sociology, Law Society & Justice, Human Rights: Law & Philosophy). The label names biomedical foundations first for the dominant disease-science anchor and patient-centred care second for the psychology/communication cluster that mirrors the comparator's own Domein I/II/III/VI structure at a general, non-clinical level.

alternatives.concept: A genuinely different second UCR route evidenced by seven generator-eligible programme-interest rows that specifically name care for patients of different ages and backgrounds (5375), accessible and inclusive dental care (5376), how socioeconomic conditions affect oral health (5377), diversity in oral healthcare (5378), multidisciplinary healthcare teamwork (5379), preventive care for vulnerable older people (5383, a Stable study direction) and social responsibility in oral healthcare (5384, a Direct programme interest) as recurring foci of the current programme, independently corroborated by VU's own current news coverage (checked 2026-09-27) of ACTA dental students making home visits to provide preventive oral care to vulnerable elderly patients using a dedicated 'oral care bike': a concentration retaining a light shared biomedical-and-patient-psychology core but replacing the closest match's disease-specialist depth and clinical-communication breadth with UCR's full available sociology, comparative-politics, ethics, leadership/diversity-management, public-economics and data-science offerings, studying how socioeconomic conditions, diversity and institutional structures shape access to, and the organisation of, oral healthcare for underserved and vulnerable populations.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum retains a light biomedical anchor (4 of 24: Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Epidemiology & Public Health, Infection & Immunity, Mechanisms of Disease) and a patient-care psychology anchor (5 of 24: Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Social Psychology, Medical & Health Psychology, Abnormal Psychology), but replaces the closest match's disease-specialist biomedical breadth and clinical-communication courses with UCR's full available sociology, comparative-politics, ethics, leadership/diversity, public-economics and data-science offerings (11 of 24: Modern Sociology, Social Movements & Environmental Justice, New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Ethics, Leadership & Diversity Management, Persuasive Communication, Introduction to Data Science, Mathematical Methods, Public Economics), plus Research Methods & Statistics, Introduction to Sociology, Law Society & Justice and Human Rights: Law & Philosophy. The label names oral health equity first for the dominant social-determinants-and-access cluster, access second for the public-policy/economics thread on funding and service organisation, and care for vulnerable populations third for the diversity-management and lifespan-psychology-adjacent courses addressing underserved and diverse patient groups.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: ACTA's current news coverage and 'Inhoud' page name social responsibility for vulnerable and diverse patient groups (accessible and inclusive care, socioeconomic determinants of oral health, care for patients of different ages and backgrounds, multidisciplinary teamwork) as a recurring, currently active strand of the programme's own professional identity, independently corroborated by seven generator-eligible programme-interest rows (5375, 5376, 5377, 5378, 5379, 5383, 5384) rather than merely by career outcomes. The closest match already includes a light societal-context thread (Introduction to Sociology, Law Society & Justice, Human Rights: Law & Philosophy -- 3 of 24 courses) reflecting the comparator's own Domein IV maatschappelijk-handelen content, but this alternative goes materially further: it retains a light shared biomedical anchor (Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Epidemiology & Public Health, Infection & Immunity, Mechanisms of Disease) and patient-psychology anchor (Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Social Psychology, Medical & Health Psychology) -- 8 of 24 courses shared with the closest match beyond the shared societal-context thread -- but replaces 11 of the closest match's remaining courses (Functional Anatomy, Molecular Cell Biology, Human Physiology, Biochemistry, Life Science Laboratory, Pharmacology, Molecular Pathology & Genetics, Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, The Art of Rhetorical Communication, Rhetoric in Action) with UCR's Modern Sociology, Social Movements & Environmental Justice, New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Ethics, Leadership & Diversity Management, Persuasive Communication, Introduction to Data Science, Mathematical Methods, Abnormal Psychology and Public Economics, for a total of eleven sociology/policy/ethics/leadership/data-science courses concentrating the programme on the social organisation of, and access to, oral healthcare. This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from a generalist biomedical-science-and-patient-care programme to a single-domain health-equity-and-access concentration, and the two alternatives share 13 of 24 courses while differing in 11 of 24 each way (82.5 EC), comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum.

progressionAssessment.rationale: HCBGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precedes Functional Anatomy, Molecular Cell Biology, Infection & Immunity (semester 4), Pharmacology, Molecular Pathology & Genetics (semester 5) and Life Science Laboratory, Mechanisms of Disease (semester 6), and Human Physiology, Biochemistry (semester 3), all of which formally require it. HCBGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies (semester 4), Medical & Health Psychology (semester 5) and Lifespan Developmental Psychology (semester 6), which formally require it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Gateway and level-1/level-2 foundational courses (Epidemiology & Public Health, Introduction to Sociology, Law Society & Justice, Research Methods & Statistics, Social Psychology, Human Physiology, Biochemistry, Statistics & Experimental Methods, The Art of Rhetorical Communication) are concentrated in semesters 1-3, and level-3 advanced disease/biomedical and psychology work (Pharmacology, Molecular Pathology & Genetics, Medical & Health Psychology, Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies, Mechanisms of Disease, Lifespan Developmental Psychology) is concentrated in semesters 4-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match directly owns thirteen generator-eligible rows: improving people's oral health (5362); looking beyond teeth to the whole patient (5363); combining healthcare, science and technology (5364); diagnosing oral-health problems (5365); planning treatment with patients (5366); preventive oral healthcare (5367); clinical problem-solving (5368); evidence-based dental care (5369); clinical dental skills (5370); precision and manual dental techniques (5371); communicating confidently with patients (5372); empathetic and respectful patient care (5373); and helping patients change health behaviour (5374). These describe the programme's own general biomedical-science core, scientific method and patient-communication orientation rather than an independent substantive direction, and are therefore substantively covered by the closest match's own core concept rather than forced into a residual candidate; note that 5370 and 5371 (clinical dental skills; precision and manual dental techniques) are honestly recorded as core-field evidence that the closest match's curriculum cannot implement through any UCR course, since UCR provides no clinical placement or dental-manual-skills practicum of any kind, and this genuine limitation is preserved rather than compensated with a weak match. The remaining seven generator-eligible rows were independently assessed as one coherent candidate direction, 'Oral Health Equity, Access and Care for Vulnerable Populations' (5375, 5376, 5377, 5378, 5379, 5383, 5384), independently corroborated by VU's own current news coverage of ACTA students providing preventive oral care to vulnerable elderly patients. This candidate passes all four gates: it is evidence-backed by seven generator-eligible rows independently corroborated by the programme's own current official news coverage as an actively practised part of its professional identity; it has a clear organising logic (concentrating on the social determinants of, and access to, oral healthcare rather than its biomedical mechanisms); it is substantively distinct, replacing 11 of the closest match's 24 courses (82.5 EC) with UCR's own sociology, policy, ethics, leadership and data-science offerings, materially changing the alternative's academic priorities; and it is mechanically feasible against the enriched course database, with six distinct level-300 courses and a pairwise difference of 11 courses (82.5 EC) against the closest match, comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course floor. Production therefore includes it as the second alternative. No further generator-eligible evidence remains to support a third genuinely distinct direction: the only remaining thin signal, combining healthcare, science and technology (5364), is already substantively covered by the closest match's own biomedical-science core and by the second alternative's data-science courses, and does not by itself support an independent, coherent third organising concept distinct from both already-included alternatives. Production therefore stops at two alternatives and records insufficient-evidence as the stopping reason for a third.

notes.text: ACTA's Bachelor Tandheelkunde combines biomedical science with extensive supervised preclinical and clinical training in diagnosing, planning and delivering dental treatment with precision and manual skill -- the Lijn TVI/TVIIA/TVIIB/TVIII skills lines and associated patient-treatment components that account for a large share of its 180 EC. At UCR, students can approach oral and systemic health through related disciplines such as biomedical science, medical and health psychology, and public health, but UCR offers no clinical placement, patient-treatment training or dental-manual-skills practicum of any kind. Both UCR alternatives therefore offer related scientific and social perspectives on oral health rather than reproducing the comparator's own clinical dental-practice curriculum.

The closest-match alternative includes substantial study of the comparator's shared biomedical-science core (cell/tissue biology, anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, infection/immunity and disease mechanisms). The comparator additionally includes dental-specialist components -- restorative crown and bridge technique, dedicated periodontal-disease treatment (Parodontitis I and II), occlusion and jaw-joint function, and dental radiography -- that UCR does not offer at the same level of depth or in clinical form; UCR students can instead combine adjacent biomedical, pharmacological and pathology coursework, but those specialist clinical components are not reproduced.
